authoredPrompt: This figure places two three-dimensional electromagnetic wave diagrams side by side along one horizontal propagation line that ends at the right in a green arrowhead labeled c. In each, the electric field is a red sinusoid oscillating in the vertical plane, filled with a comb of short arrows running from the axis up to the curve, while the magnetic field is a matching blue sinusoid in the horizontal plane, drawn in perspective as flattened lobes with arrows of its own. Pale teal square panels stand upright along the axis so the two perpendicular oscillation planes stay legible. The left wave is the smaller; black leaders at its left end label the red curve E and the blue curve B, and the symbol u sits above it. The right wave carries visibly taller red lobes and wider blue lobes over the same wavelength, its leaders read 2E and 2B, and the label above it is 4u. Drawing both on a single axis at identical wavelength isolates amplitude as the only difference, so the paired labels above carry the comparison. The figure introduces amplitude as what governs the energy an electromagnetic wave stores and transports.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for field amplitude: the learner drags amplitude from E,B to 2E,2B, the red and blue wave heights grow while the energy-density label changes quadratically, showing why doubling both fields produces four times the energy density.
- Animation for propagation: the learner plays the wave moving along the c arrow, the perpendicular E and B oscillations advance together, clarifying that electromagnetic energy flux travels in the propagation direction while the fields remain transverse.
- Toggle between field view and energy view: the learner switches from the E/B wave diagram to shaded energy-density panels, making the relationship between field amplitude and transported energy visible without changing wavelength.
authoredContext:
Clearly, the larger the strength of the electric and magnetic fields, the more work they can do and the greater the energy the electromagnetic wave carries. In electromagnetic waves, the amplitude is the maximum field strength of the electric and magnetic fields (the figure). The wave energy is determined by the wave amplitude.

Energy carried by a wave depends on its amplitude. With electromagnetic waves, doubling the E fields and B fields quadruples the energy density u and the energy flux uc.

Figure on the left shows an electromagnetic wave with electric field E and magnetic field B. It is labeled u. Figure on the right shows an electromagnetic wave with electric field 2E and magnetic field 2B. Here, the amplitudes of the sine waves are doubled. The wave is labeled 4u.
